name: MaterializedView
purpose: Maintains a pre-computed query result kept up to date by an incremental feed so read queries never recompute from base tables.
api_signature:
from typing import Protocol, Any, Iterable

class MaterializedView(Protocol):
    @property
    def name(self) -> str: ...
    def apply(self, event: Any) -> None: ...
    def rebuild(self, source: Iterable[Any]) -> None: ...
    def query(self, criteria: object) -> Iterable[Any]: ...
invariants: apply MUST be deterministic: given the same event stream in the same order, the view state SHALL converge to the same contents.
The view CANNOT be the system of record; rebuild MUST be able to regenerate state purely from the source feed.
Reads against the view MUST tolerate bounded staleness and NEVER claim linearizability with the base data.
Schema evolution SHALL trigger a rebuild path; silent backfill with stale rows is FORBIDDEN.
extension_contract: New projections extend MaterializedView by subclassing the Protocol and registering event-handler functions via a decorator per aggregate type; storage backends plug in through an adapter interface so the same projection can target OLTP, OLAP, or a search index.

sources.locator: Chapter 11, Stream Processing, materialized views, pp. 461-466
Chapter 7, CQRS and materialized views, pp. 253-278

why_essential: Without a shared primitive, each tool builds its own cache-or-view with divergent invalidation rules and nobody can tell which rows are stale when a customer disputes a balance.
alternatives_considered: On-demand recomputation: unbounded latency for hot reads.
Hand-rolled caches with TTL: stale forever on missed invalidations.
OLAP cube refresh nightly: too coarse for operational reads.
